name: Bon soup
summary: Thái bon soup, and the accounts do not use one pot. Vietnamnet, on 16 March 2019, uses young sweet bon, the plant also called khoai nước, with a purple spot on the leaf, peeled and soaked to lose its sap, plus mắc khén and buffalo or beef skin that was dried on the hearth, burned until it puffs, scraped to yellow, soaked soft, and cooked until tender. Báo Sơn La, on 4 September 2020, names lá bon, wild eggplant, chili, mắc khén, onion, bạc nhạc bò or beef, salt, mì chính, and lá lốt, soaked in light salt water and cooked with beef or beef bone. On 2 July 2021 the same paper names buffalo skin and cà dại. All three stay.
origin: Vietnamnet, 16 March 2019. Báo Sơn La, 4 September 2020 and 2 July 2021.
taste: Báo Sơn La, on 4 September 2020, names mắc khén, the bùi richness of bon, chili heat, and the sweetness of the meat. Vietnamnet does not print that taste line.
howToEat: As the soup. An hour and a price are Check on arrival. A simmer time was not in the Vietnamnet or Báo Sơn La accounts read here.
where: Thái households, and the ethnic restaurants Vietnamnet mentions without naming one. No shop is a pick.
seoTitle: Canh bon in Son La — skin in one pot, beef in another
seoDescription: Canh bon in Sơn La. Vietnamnet uses hearth-dried buffalo or beef skin. Báo Sơn La uses beef or beef bone, and also names buffalo skin and cà dại. A price is Check on arrival.
